source.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ἕν, καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον·

records.literal_gloss: On the next day the crowd, the [one] having stood on the other side of the sea, saw that boat other not was there except one, and that not went in with the disciples of him the Jesus into the boat, but alone the disciples of him went away;

en.L: On the next day the crowd that was standing on the other side of the sea saw that no other small boat had been there except one, and that Jesus had not gone into the boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples had gone away alone.
en.B: The next day the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea saw that there had been only one boat there, and that Jesus had not gone on board with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. The disciples had left by themselves.
en.R: The next day the crowd was still on the other side of the lake. They knew that only one boat had been there. They also knew that Jesus had not gotten into it with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. The disciples had left without {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Al día siguiente, la multitud que estaba al otro lado del mar vio que allí no había habido otra barca sino una, y que Jesús no había entrado en la barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, sino que {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se habían ido solos.
es.B: Al día siguiente, la multitud que seguía al otro lado del mar vio que allí solo había habido una barca, y que Jesús no había subido a ella con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Los discípulos se habían ido solos.
es.R: Al día siguiente, la gente seguía al otro lado del lago. Sabía que allí solo había habido una barca. Sabía también que Jesús no había subido a ella con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Los discípulos se habían ido sin {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Le lendemain, la foule qui se tenait de l’autre côté de la mer vit qu’il n’y avait eu là aucune autre petite barque, sauf une, et que Jésus n’était pas monté dans la barque avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, mais que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples étaient partis seuls.
fr.B: Le lendemain, la foule restée de l’autre côté de la mer constata qu’il n’y avait eu là qu’une seule barque, et que Jésus n’y était pas monté avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Les disciples étaient partis seuls.
fr.R: Le lendemain, la foule était toujours de l’autre côté du lac. Les gens savaient qu’il n’y avait eu là qu’une seule barque. Ils savaient aussi que Jésus n’y était pas monté avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Les disciples étaient partis sans {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kesho yake umati uliokuwa umesimama ng'ambo ya bahari uliona kwamba hapakuwa na mashua nyingine ndogo pale isipokuwa moja, na kwamba Yesu hakuwa ameingia mashuani pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, bali wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wameondoka peke yao.
sw.B: Kesho yake umati uliokuwa umebaki ng'ambo ya bahari uliona kwamba palikuwa na mashua moja tu pale, na kwamba Yesu hakuwa amepanda pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Wanafunzi walikuwa wameondoka peke yao.
sw.R: Kesho yake umati ulikuwa bado upande wa pili wa ziwa. Walijua kwamba palikuwa na mashua moja tu pale. Walijua pia kwamba Yesu hakuwa ameingia ndani yake pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Wanafunzi walikuwa wameondoka bila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

vi.L: Ngày hôm sau, đoàn dân đứng ở bên kia biển thấy rằng ở đó không có chiếc thuyền nhỏ nào khác ngoài một chiếc, và Đức Giê-xu đã không cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống thuyền, nhưng chỉ các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi mà thôi.
vi.B: Ngày hôm sau, đoàn dân còn ở lại bên kia biển nhận thấy rằng chỉ có một chiếc thuyền ở đó, và Đức Giê-xu đã không lên thuyền cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Các môn đồ đã đi riêng.
vi.R: Ngày hôm sau, dân chúng vẫn còn ở bờ bên kia hồ. Họ biết chỉ có một chiếc thuyền ở đó. Họ cũng biết Đức Giê-xu đã không lên thuyền với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Các môn đồ đã đi mà không có {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그다음 날, 바다 건너편에 서 있던 무리는 그곳에 작은 배 한 척 외에는 다른 배가 없었다는 것과, 예수께서 그분의 제자들과 함께 그 배에 오르지 않으셨고 그분의 제자들만 떠나갔다는 것을 보았다.
ko.B: 이튿날, 바다 건너편에 남아 있던 무리는 그곳에 배가 한 척밖에 없었다는 것과, 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그 배에 오르지 않으셨다는 것을 알았다. 제자들만 떠났던 것이다.
ko.R: 다음 날에도 무리는 아직 호수 건너편에 있었다. 그들은 그곳에 배가 한 척밖에 없었다는 것을 알고 있었다. 또 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그 배에 타지 않으셨다는 것도 알고 있었다. 제자들은 예수 없이 떠났던 것이다.

pt.L: No dia seguinte, a multidão que estava do outro lado do mar viu que não havia ali nenhum outro barquinho, a não ser um, e que Jesus não tinha entrado no barco com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos, mas os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos tinham partido sozinhos.
pt.B: No dia seguinte, a multidão que tinha ficado do outro lado do mar viu que só havia um barco ali e que Jesus não tinha embarcado com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos. Os discípulos tinham partido sozinhos.
pt.R: No dia seguinte, a multidão ainda estava do outro lado do lago. As pessoas sabiam que só havia um barco ali. Também sabiam que Jesus não tinha entrado nele com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos. Os discípulos tinham ido embora sem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

decisions.choice: a long sentence that sets the scene; the story picks it up again in 6:24
decisions.reason: John piles up what the crowd had noticed: only one boat had been there the evening before, and Jesus had not gone off in it with his disciples (6:16-17). The sentence then breaks off; 6:23 adds a remark about other boats, and 6:24 starts again with "so when the crowd saw". The point of it all is the crowd's puzzle: Jesus had not left by boat, yet he was gone. They know nothing of his walking on the sea (6:19-21).

decisions.choice: the other side of the sea: the shore where the crowd had been fed
decisions.reason: The crowd stayed on the far side of the Sea of Galilee from Capernaum, where Jesus had fed them (6:1-13). The same phrase in 6:25 means the opposite shore, around Capernaum: John speaks from wherever the crowd is not.

decisions.choice: except one (SBLGNT)
alternatives: except that one into which his disciples had got (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts end the clause with "one". Many later ones add words saying which boat this was, the one the disciples had taken; the addition explains the sentence but does not change its sense. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: two sentences (B); five short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence is tangled (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable break it where the thought allows; Literal keeps it whole. Readable says "without him" for "alone", which is what "alone" means here.

decisions.choice: lake
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake; Readable uses the plain word so a young reader does not picture the ocean. 6:25 does the same.

decisions.choice: two sentences (B); short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the Greek sentence is tangled (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable break it where the thought allows. Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John’s present tense where he uses it; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (6:22-40), as in 6:1-21. The passé simple ("vit", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus a répondu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Jesus’s long answer is speech, so it uses the present and the passé composé at every level ("vous avez vu", "je suis descendu").

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}}, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God takes the deity_pronoun setting, including "me", "moi", "mon" when Jesus speaks of himself and "tu", "te", "toi" when people speak to him; "je" has none, and a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital. A possessive agrees with the noun ("sa volonté", "mon Père"). This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans; "그분" with the honorific "-시-" and "께서"
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and the Father is carried by the subject honorific and "그분" at every level. This holds for the whole passage.

records.literal_gloss: But came boats from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread, having given thanks the Lord.

en.L: But small boats came from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
en.B: Some boats from Tiberias, however, came in near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks.
en.R: But some boats from the town of Tiberias came to shore near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks for it.

es.L: Pero llegaron barcas de Tiberíades cerca del lugar donde comieron el pan después de que el Señor dio gracias.
es.B: Sin embargo, llegaron unas barcas de Tiberíades cerca del lugar donde habían comido el pan después de que el Señor dio gracias.
es.R: Pero algunas barcas de la ciudad de Tiberíades llegaron a la orilla cerca del lugar donde la gente había comido el pan después de que el Señor dio gracias por él.

fr.L: Mais de petites barques vinrent de Tibériade près du lieu où ils mangèrent le pain après que le Seigneur eut rendu grâce.
fr.B: Cependant, des barques venues de Tibériade arrivèrent près de l’endroit où l’on avait mangé le pain après que le Seigneur eut rendu grâce.
fr.R: Mais des barques de la ville de Tibériade sont arrivées près de l’endroit où les gens avaient mangé le pain, après que le Seigneur avait remercié Dieu pour ce pain.

sw.L: Lakini mashua ndogo zilikuja kutoka Tiberia karibu na mahali walipokula mkate baada ya Bwana kushukuru.

vi.L: Nhưng có những chiếc thuyền nhỏ từ Ti-bê-ri-át đến gần nơi họ đã ăn bánh sau khi Chúa tạ ơn.
vi.B: Tuy nhiên, có mấy chiếc thuyền từ Ti-bê-ri-át đến gần chỗ họ đã ăn bánh sau khi Chúa tạ ơn.
vi.R: Nhưng có mấy chiếc thuyền từ thành Ti-bê-ri-át đến cập bờ gần nơi dân chúng đã ăn bánh, sau khi Chúa cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러나 디베랴에서 작은 배들이, 주님께서 감사를 드리신 후에 그들이 빵을 먹었던 곳 가까이로 왔다.
ko.B: 그런데 디베랴에서 온 배 몇 척이, 주님께서 감사를 드리신 뒤 사람들이 빵을 먹었던 곳 가까이에 와 닿았다.
ko.R: 그런데 디베랴라는 도시에서 배 몇 척이 와서, 주님께서 감사 기도를 드리신 뒤 사람들이 빵을 먹었던 곳 가까이에 닿았다.

pt.L: Mas vieram barquinhos de Tiberíades, perto do lugar onde comeram o pão depois que o Senhor deu graças.
pt.B: Alguns barcos de Tiberíades, porém, chegaram perto do lugar onde tinham comido o pão depois que o Senhor deu graças.
pt.R: Mas alguns barcos da cidade de Tiberíades chegaram à margem perto do lugar onde o povo tinha comido o pão depois que o Senhor deu graças por ele.

decisions.choice: after the Lord had given thanks (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Nearly all manuscripts have the phrase. A few witnesses leave it out, among them Codex Bezae and some early Latin and Syriac versions. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the narrator's name for Jesus, recalling the meal
decisions.reason: John's narrative rarely calls Jesus "the Lord" before the resurrection (also 4:1 and 11:2); after it, the disciples do so often (20:20; 21:7, 12). Here the thanksgiving of 6:11 is singled out as the mark of that meal: the bread was eaten after he gave thanks.

decisions.choice: Tiberias: the new city on the west shore
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas founded Tiberias on the west shore of the lake about AD 20 and named it after the emperor Tiberius. John has already called the lake "the Sea of Tiberias" (6:1; also 21:1). Boats from there give the crowd a way across.

decisions.choice: but: boats did come, though Jesus had not left by boat
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts are written without accents, so the same letters can be read as "but" or as "other" ("other boats came"). The SBLGNT reads "but", setting these boats against the single boat of 6:22. Either way the sense is the same: there were now boats for the crowd.

decisions.choice: had eaten (B, R); the people (R)
decisions.reason: English needs the earlier past for a meal that happened the day before. Readable names who ate, since "they" could be taken as the people on the boats.

decisions.choice: the town of Tiberias; came to shore; for it
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tiberias was a town, that the boats landed, and what the thanks were for (6:11).

decisions.choice: la ciudad de Tiberíades; llegaron a la orilla; por él
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what Tiberias was, that the boats landed, and what the thanks were for.

decisions.choice: le Seigneur ... eut rendu grâce (L, B); avait remercié Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: "Le Seigneur" is the narrator’s title for Jesus (meaning decision m2), kept at every level. The verb is rendered as in 6:11, "rendre grâce" at Literal and Balanced and "remercier Dieu" at Readable, so the reader recognises the meal.

decisions.choice: "주님" for the narrator's "the Lord"
decisions.reason: The narrator's title for Jesus is "주님" at every level (docs/john-terms.md), with the subject honorific "께서".

source.text: ὅτε οὖν εἶδεν ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, ἐνέβησαν αὐτοὶ εἰς τὰ πλοιάρια καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ ζητοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore saw the crowd that Jesus not is there nor the disciples of him, got in they into the boats and came to Capernaum seeking the Jesus.

en.L: So when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
en.B: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The crowd saw that Jesus was not there, and that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were not there either. So they got into those boats and went across to Capernaum to look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Cuando, pues, la multitud vio que Jesús no estaba allí, ni {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, subieron ellos mismos a las barcas y fueron a Capernaúm buscando a Jesús.
es.B: Así que, cuando la gente vio que ni Jesús ni {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos estaban allí, subieron a las barcas y fueron a Capernaúm a buscarlo.
es.R: La gente vio que Jesús no estaba allí, y que {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos tampoco. Entonces subieron a esas barcas y cruzaron hasta Capernaúm para buscarlo.

fr.L: Quand donc la foule vit que Jésus n’était pas là, ni {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, ils montèrent eux-mêmes dans les barques et vinrent à Capharnaüm, cherchant Jésus.
fr.B: Quand la foule vit que ni Jésus ni {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples n’étaient là, les gens montèrent dans les barques et allèrent à Capharnaüm pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher.
fr.R: La foule a vu que Jésus n’était pas là, et que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples n’y étaient pas non plus. Alors les gens sont montés dans ces barques et ils ont traversé jusqu’à Capharnaüm pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher.

sw.L: Basi umati ulipoona kwamba Yesu hayuko pale, wala wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wao wenyewe waliingia katika mashua, wakaja Kapernaumu, wakimtafuta Yesu.
sw.B: Basi umati ulipoona kwamba Yesu hayupo pale wala wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, waliingia katika mashua, wakaenda Kapernaumu kumtafuta.
sw.R: Umati uliona kwamba Yesu hakuwepo pale, na kwamba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} pia hawakuwepo. Basi waliingia katika mashua zile, wakavuka kwenda Kapernaumu kumtafuta.

vi.L: Vậy khi đoàn dân thấy Đức Giê-xu không có ở đó, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng không, thì chính họ xuống những chiếc thuyền nhỏ ấy và đến Ca-bê-na-um, tìm Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Vậy khi đoàn dân thấy cả Đức Giê-xu lẫn các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều không có ở đó, họ xuống mấy chiếc thuyền ấy và đi đến Ca-bê-na-um tìm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Dân chúng thấy Đức Giê-xu không có ở đó, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng không. Vì vậy, họ lên mấy chiếc thuyền ấy và đi qua Ca-bê-na-um để tìm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그래서 무리는 예수께서 거기 계시지 않고 그분의 제자들도 없는 것을 보고, 그들 자신이 그 작은 배들에 올라 예수를 찾으며 가버나움으로 갔다.
ko.B: 무리는 예수께서 거기 계시지 않고 제자들도 없는 것을 보고, 그 배들을 타고 예수를 찾아 가버나움으로 갔다.
ko.R: 무리는 예수께서 거기 계시지 않고 제자들도 없는 것을 보았다. 그래서 그 배들을 타고 예수를 찾으러 호수 건너 가버나움으로 갔다.

pt.L: Então, quando a multidão viu que Jesus não estava ali, nem os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos, eles mesmos entraram nos barquinhos e foram para Cafarnaum, procurando Jesus.
pt.B: Então, quando a multidão viu que nem Jesus nem os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos estavam ali, entrou nos barcos e foi para Cafarnaum à procura {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: A multidão viu que Jesus não estava ali e que os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos também não. Então as pessoas entraram naqueles barcos e atravessaram até Cafarnaum para procurá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.

decisions.choice: so when: the story picks up from 6:22
decisions.reason: The word translated "so" takes up the thread that 6:22 left hanging, after the remark about the boats in 6:23. The crowd has waited and searched, and now gives up on the shore where they ate.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: where Jesus had made his home
decisions.reason: Jesus had stayed in Capernaum with his mother, brothers and disciples (2:12), and his disciples had set out for it the evening before (6:17). It was the obvious place to look. 6:59 says the following talk took place in the synagogue there.

decisions.choice: seeking Jesus: the word Jesus takes up in his reply
decisions.reason: John says the crowd came "seeking" Jesus, and Jesus answers by asking why they seek him (6:26). In John, seeking can be true or false: the first disciples are asked "What are you seeking?" (1:38), and some seek Jesus to kill him (7:1).

decisions.choice: neither Jesus nor his disciples were there
alternatives: Jesus was not there, nor his disciples (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two names in one phrase, as English does; Literal keeps the Greek order, which adds the disciples as an afterthought.

decisions.choice: to look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: "Seeking" is less common in speech; "look for" is the everyday word. Balanced and Readable say "him", since Jesus was named just before.

decisions.choice: buscar
decisions.reason: The word Jesus takes up in his reply (6:26), so every level keeps "buscar".

decisions.choice: chercher
decisions.reason: French "chercher" is both the everyday verb and the word of Jesus’s reply in 6:26 ("vous me cherchez") and of 1:38 ("Que cherchez-vous ?"), so every level keeps it and the thread noted in meaning decision m3 stays visible.

source.text: Καὶ εὑρόντες αὐτὸν πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶπον αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, πότε ὧδε γέγονας;

records.literal_gloss: And having found him on the other side of the sea they said to him, "Rabbi, when here have you come?"

en.L: And having found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the other side of the sea, they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, when did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come here?"
en.B: When they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the other side of the sea, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, when did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} get here?"
en.R: They found Jesus on the other side of the lake and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, when did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} get here?"

es.L: Y al encontrarlo al otro lado del mar, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Rabí, ¿cuándo llegaste acá?».
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron al otro lado del mar, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Rabí, ¿cuándo llegaste aquí?».
es.R: Encontraron a Jesús al otro lado del lago y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Rabí, ¿cuándo llegaste aquí?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant trouvé de l’autre côté de la mer, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Rabbi, quand es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} arrivé ici ? »
fr.B: Quand ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}eurent trouvé de l’autre côté de la mer, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandèrent : « Rabbi, quand es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} arrivé ici ? »
fr.R: Ils ont trouvé Jésus de l’autre côté du lac, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Rabbi, quand est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es arrivé ici ? »

sw.L: Na walipomkuta ng'ambo ya bahari, wakamwambia, "Rabi, ulifika lini huku?"
sw.B: Walipomkuta ng'ambo ya bahari, wakamwuliza, "Rabi, umefika lini hapa?"
sw.R: Walimkuta Yesu upande wa pili wa ziwa, wakamwuliza, "Rabi, umefika lini hapa?"

vi.L: Khi tìm thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở bên kia biển, họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, Thầy đến đây khi nào?"
vi.B: Khi tìm gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở bên kia biển, họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, Thầy đến đây bao giờ vậy?"
vi.R: Họ tìm thấy Đức Giê-xu ở bờ bên kia hồ và hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, Thầy đến đây lúc nào vậy?"

ko.L: 그리고 바다 건너편에서 그분을 찾아내고, 그분께 말하였다. "랍비, 언제 여기 오셨습니까?"
ko.B: 그들은 바다 건너편에서 그분을 찾아내고 물었다. "랍비님, 언제 이리로 오셨습니까?"
ko.R: 그들은 호수 건너편에서 예수를 찾아내고 물었다. "랍비님, 언제 여기 오셨습니까?"

pt.L: E, tendo-{{deity_pronoun:o|O}} encontrado do outro lado do mar, {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Rabi, quando vieste para cá?"
pt.B: Quando {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} encontraram do outro lado do mar, {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntaram: "Rabi, quando chegaste aqui?"
pt.R: Eles encontraram Jesus do outro lado do lago e perguntaram a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Rabi, quando chegaste aqui?"

decisions.choice: when did you come here: they ask about the time, wondering how he crossed
decisions.reason: The question is "when", but behind it is the puzzle of 6:22: there had been no boat for him. The perfect tense asks how long he has been here. Jesus does not answer it; he turns to why they are looking for him (6:26). The crowd knows nothing of what happened on the sea in the night (6:19-21).

decisions.choice: Rabbi: the respectful title for a teacher
decisions.reason: The day before, this crowd called Jesus "the prophet" and wanted to make him king (6:14-15). Now they address him with the ordinary title for a teacher, which John explained at 1:38.

decisions.choice: the other side of the sea: the Capernaum shore
decisions.reason: Seen from where they had been fed, Capernaum is on the other side (see the note at 6:22).

decisions.choice: Rabbi
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: John translates the word himself (1:38), so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: get here
decisions.reason: The everyday way of asking about someone's arrival.

decisions.choice: "랍비" (L); "랍비님" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps John's word; as an address Balanced and Readable add the honorific "-님" that Korean expects.

decisions.choice: the crowd speaks to Jesus in the formal style (합쇼체: "오셨습니까", "주십시오")
decisions.reason: The style guide sets 합쇼체 for people speaking to Jesus; Jesus answers in the plain style (해라체: "말한다", "하여라"). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: the crowd calls Jesus "Thầy" and itself "chúng tôi"; Jesus calls the crowd "các người"
decisions.reason: The crowd has just addressed him as Rabbi, "teacher", so "Thầy" (which the style guide allows for others who respect him) fits better than "ông" and is kept through 6:25-34. "Thầy" is a noun of address, so it takes no deity_pronoun span where the English "you" has one.

decisions.choice: tu (vieste, chegaste; and in 6:30, 6:34)
decisions.reason: The crowd speaks to Jesus with "tu", as everyone who addresses Jesus does in this translation (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); their attitude shows in their words, not in the form of address. The English deity_pronoun span on "you" has no counterpart where Portuguese leaves the pronoun in the verb ending.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητεῖτέ με οὐχ ὅτι εἴδετε σημεῖα ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐφάγετε ἐκ τῶν ἄρτων καὶ ἐχορτάσθητε·

records.literal_gloss: Answered them the Jesus and said, "Truly truly I say to you, you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled;

en.L: Jesus answered them and said, "Truly, truly I say to you, you are seeking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, you are looking for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: you are not looking for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because you saw what the signs meant. You are looking for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because you ate the bread and were full.

es.L: Jesús les respondió y dijo: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}, no porque {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} señales, sino porque {{plural_you:comieron de los panes y se saciaron|comisteis de los panes y os saciasteis}}.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}, no porque {{plural_you:hayan visto|hayáis visto}} señales, sino porque {{plural_you:comieron pan hasta llenarse|comisteis pan hasta llenaros}}.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} porque {{plural_you:hayan entendido|hayáis entendido}} lo que significaban las señales. Me {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} porque {{plural_you:comieron pan y quedaron llenos|comisteis pan y quedasteis llenos}}.

fr.L: Jésus leur répondit et dit : « En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis, vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchez non parce que vous avez vu des signes, mais parce que vous avez mangé des pains et avez été rassasiés.
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis : vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchez, non parce que vous avez vu des signes, mais parce que vous avez mangé des pains à satiété.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchez pas parce que vous avez compris ce que voulaient dire les signes. Vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} cherchez parce que vous avez mangé du pain et que vous avez eu le ventre plein.

sw.L: Yesu akawajibu, akasema, "Kweli kweli nawaambia, mnanitafuta, si kwa sababu mliona ishara, bali kwa sababu mlikula ile mikate mkashiba.
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Kweli kweli nawaambia, mnanitafuta, si kwa sababu mliona ishara, bali kwa sababu mlikula mikate mkashiba.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Nawaambia ukweli: hamnitafuti kwa sababu mlielewa maana ya ishara. Mnanitafuta kwa sababu mlikula mkate mkashiba.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời họ và nói: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không phải vì đã thấy các dấu lạ, nhưng vì đã ăn bánh và được no.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không phải vì đã thấy các dấu lạ, nhưng vì đã được ăn bánh no nê.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ta nói thật với các người: các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không phải vì đã hiểu ý nghĩa của các dấu lạ. Các người tìm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vì đã được ăn bánh no nê.

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희가 나를 찾는 것은 표적들을 보았기 때문이 아니라, 빵을 먹고 배가 불렀기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희가 나를 찾는 것은 표적을 보았기 때문이 아니라, 빵을 배불리 먹었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 너희가 나를 찾는 것은 표적이 무엇을 뜻하는지 알았기 때문이 아니다. 빵을 먹고 배가 불렀기 때문이다.

pt.L: Jesus lhes respondeu e disse: "Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} procuram não porque viram sinais, mas porque comeram dos pães e ficaram saciados.
pt.B: Jesus lhes respondeu: "Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} procuram não porque viram sinais, mas porque comeram dos pães até se fartar.
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Eu garanto a vocês: vocês não estão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} procurando porque viram o que os sinais significavam. Vocês estão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} procurando porque comeram o pão e ficaram de barriga cheia.

decisions.choice: saw signs: saw what the signs pointed to
decisions.reason: The crowd had watched the feeding and even called it a sign (6:14). Jesus says they did not see signs: they saw a meal, not what it pointed to, who he is and what he gives. In John a sign is meant to lead to believing (2:11; 20:30-31). The plural takes in the healings that drew the crowd in the first place (6:2).

decisions.choice: were filled: had full stomachs
decisions.reason: ἐχορτάσθητε is a plain word for eating until one is full; it was first used of feeding animals. It is the word of 6:12 ("when they were filled"). Jesus sets their full stomachs against the signs they missed.

decisions.choice: you are seeking me: an ongoing search
decisions.reason: The present tense describes what they have been doing since the morning (6:22-24). The same verb ends 6:24.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:32 as well.

decisions.choice: ate your fill (B); saw what the signs meant ... were full (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for being filled. Readable spells out what "seeing signs" means here (meaning decision m1) and repeats "you are looking for me" to keep the two reasons apart.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:32 as well.

decisions.choice: hayan entendido lo que significaban las señales
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out what "seeing signs" means here (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
alternatives: Amen, amen, je vous le dis
Oui, vraiment, je vous le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:32 as well. Readable puts the pledge in plain words.

decisions.choice: avez été rassasiés
decisions.reason: The verb of 6:12 ("quand ils furent rassasiés"), so Literal uses the same French word; Balanced says "à satiété" and Readable "le ventre plein" for the plain picture of full stomachs (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice (style guide); the archaic "이르노니" is avoided. This holds for the whole passage (6:26, 6:32).

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Vietnamese rendering of "amen, amen", recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:32 as well.

decisions.choice: "nói" for Jesus speaking, at every level
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice (docs/vietnamese-style.md), settled in October 2026: the narrator introduces Jesus's words with the everyday verb, as it does for every other speaker, so the narrative stays modern and the three levels agree; "phán", the reverential verb, is kept for God speaking (1:33; 9:29; 12:28).

decisions.choice: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo (L, B); Eu garanto a vocês (R)
decisions.reason: John's doubled formula as docs/portuguese-style.md section 6 sets it, recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:32 as well.

source.text: ἐργάζεσθε μὴ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν ἀπολλυμένην ἀλλὰ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν μένουσαν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἣν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑμῖν δώσει, τοῦτον γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐσφράγισεν ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: Work not [for] the food the perishing, but [for] the food the remaining to life eternal, which the Son of the Man to you will give; this one for the Father sealed, the God.

en.L: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you; for the Father, God, has sealed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Do not work for food that passes away, but for the food that remains for eternal life, the food the Son of Man will give you. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one God the Father has marked with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seal."
en.R: Do not work hard for food that goes bad. Work for the food that lasts and gives eternal life, the life of the age to come, which starts now. The Son of Man will give you this food, because God the Father has put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seal on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. That seal shows that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes from God."

es.L: No {{plural_you:trabajen|trabajéis}} por la comida que se pierde, sino por la comida que permanece para vida eterna, la cual el Hijo del Hombre {{plural_you:les|os}} dará; porque a este {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha sellado el Padre, Dios».
es.B: No {{plural_you:trabajen|trabajéis}} por la comida que se echa a perder, sino por la comida que permanece para vida eterna, la que el Hijo del Hombre {{plural_you:les|os}} dará. Porque a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} Dios el Padre {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha marcado con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sello».
es.R: No {{plural_you:trabajen|trabajéis}} por la comida que se echa a perder. {{plural_you:Trabajen|Trabajad}} por la comida que dura y da vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya. El Hijo del Hombre {{plural_you:les|os}} dará esa comida, porque Dios el Padre ha puesto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sello sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Ese sello muestra que viene de Dios».

fr.L: Travaillez non pour la nourriture qui se perd, mais pour la nourriture qui demeure pour la vie éternelle, que le Fils de l’homme vous donnera ; car c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que le Père, Dieu, a marqué de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sceau. »
fr.B: Ne travaillez pas pour la nourriture qui se perd, mais pour celle qui demeure pour la vie éternelle, celle que le Fils de l’homme vous donnera. Car c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que Dieu le Père a marqué de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sceau. »
fr.R: Ne vous donnez pas tant de peine pour une nourriture qui se gâte. Travaillez pour la nourriture qui dure et qui donne la vie éternelle, la vie du monde à venir, qui commence dès maintenant. Le Fils de l’homme vous donnera cette nourriture, parce que Dieu le Père a mis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sceau sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ce sceau montre qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient de Dieu. »

sw.L: Msifanye kazi kwa ajili ya chakula kinachoharibika, bali kwa ajili ya chakula kinachodumu hadi uzima wa milele, ambacho Mwana wa Adamu atawapa; kwa maana huyo Baba, Mungu, amemtia mhuri."
sw.B: Msifanye kazi kwa ajili ya chakula kinachopita, bali kwa ajili ya chakula kinachodumu hadi uzima wa milele, chakula ambacho Mwana wa Adamu atawapa. Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye ambaye Mungu Baba amemtia mhuri {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}."
sw.R: Msijitaabishe kwa ajili ya chakula kinachooza. Fanyeni kazi kwa ajili ya chakula kinachodumu na kuleta uzima wa milele, uzima wa nyakati zijazo, unaoanza sasa. Mwana wa Adamu atawapa chakula hicho, kwa sababu Mungu Baba amemtia mhuri {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Mhuri huo unaonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anatoka kwa Mungu."

vi.L: Đừng làm việc vì thức ăn hay hư mất, nhưng vì thức ăn còn lại đến sự sống đời đời, là thức ăn mà Con Người sẽ ban cho các người; vì Cha, tức là Đức Chúa Trời, đã đóng ấn trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Đừng làm việc vì thức ăn hay hư nát, nhưng hãy làm việc vì thức ăn còn mãi đến sự sống đời đời, là thức ăn mà Con Người sẽ ban cho các người. Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đấng được Đức Chúa Trời, là Cha, đóng ấn xác nhận."
vi.R: Đừng vất vả làm việc vì thức ăn mau hư. Hãy làm việc vì thức ăn còn mãi và ban sự sống đời đời, tức là sự sống của thời đại sắp đến, bắt đầu ngay từ bây giờ. Con Người sẽ ban cho các người thức ăn ấy, vì Đức Chúa Trời, là Cha, đã đóng ấn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên Con Người. Ấn ấy cho thấy Con Người đến từ Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 썩어 없어질 양식을 위하여 일하지 말고, 영원한 생명에 이르도록 남는 양식을 위하여 일하여라. 그것은 인자가 너희에게 줄 것이다. 아버지, 곧 하나님께서 그에게 인을 치셨기 때문이다."
ko.B: 썩어 없어질 양식을 얻으려고 일하지 말고, 영원한 생명에 이르도록 오래 남는 양식을 얻으려고 일하여라. 그 양식은 인자가 너희에게 줄 것이다. 아버지 하나님께서 그에게 당신의 인을 치셨기 때문이다."
ko.R: 상해 버릴 음식을 얻으려고 애써 일하지 마라. 오래가는 음식, 영원한 생명을 주는 음식을 얻으려고 일하여라. 영원한 생명은 다가올 시대의 생명인데, 지금부터 시작된다. 인자, 곧 사람의 아들이 너희에게 이 음식을 줄 것이다. 아버지 하나님께서 그에게 도장을 찍듯이 인을 치셨기 때문이다. 그것은 그가 하나님께로부터 왔다는 표시이다."

pt.L: Trabalhem não pela comida que perece, mas pela comida que permanece para a vida eterna, a qual o Filho do Homem lhes dará; pois o Pai, Deus, {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} selou."

decisions.choice: food that perishes, food that remains: what passes away against what lasts
decisions.reason: ἀπόλλυμι is the word of 6:12, "so that nothing is lost", and of 6:39, "that I should lose none". μένουσαν is John's word "remain", which he later uses of the bond between Jesus and those who eat his bread (6:56; 15:4). The manna itself went bad if it was kept overnight (Exodus 16:20).

decisions.choice: working for food that does not satisfy
decisions.reason: The thought is close to Isaiah 55:2, which asks why people spend their money and their labor on what is not bread and cannot satisfy. There too God invites people to come and eat what gives life (Isaiah 55:1-3). Jesus is not telling them to stop earning a living but to set their hearts on the food that lasts, which in the end is a gift ("which the Son of Man will give").

decisions.choice: set his seal: marked him as his own and confirmed him
alternatives: the seal is a particular event, such as the Spirit coming down on Jesus at his baptism (1:32-33)
decisions.reason: A seal pressed into wax marked who owned something and vouched that it was genuine. God has confirmed the Son as his own and given him authority. 3:33-34 uses the same picture: whoever accepts his testimony puts a seal to it that God is true. The sentence ends with "God", placed last for weight: the Father who did this is God himself.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man will give: a gift still to come
decisions.reason: Jesus uses his title for himself (1:51; 3:13-14). The future tense looks ahead to 6:51: "the bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world".

decisions.choice: passes away ... remains (B); goes bad ... lasts (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "remains", John's recurring word (see docs/john-terms.md), and uses an everyday word for perishing. Readable uses the plainest words for food that spoils and food that does not.

decisions.choice: the life of the age to come, which starts now; That seal shows that he comes from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "eternal life" once in this passage, and says what the seal means (meaning decision m3). It turns "for" into "because" so the link between the gift and the seal is plain.

decisions.choice: se pierde (L); se echa a perder (B, R); permanece (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Perder" keeps the link with 6:12 and 6:39 (meaning decision m1), and "permanecer" is John's "remain". Readable says "dura" in plain words.

decisions.choice: la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya; Ese sello muestra que viene de Dios
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage and says what the seal means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: the quotation closes at the end of this verse
decisions.reason: Jesus's words end here and the crowd answers in 6:28. (The English leaves this quotation open.)

decisions.choice: qui se perd ... qui demeure (L, B); qui se gâte ... qui dure (R)
decisions.reason: "Se perdre" keeps the verb French uses in 6:12 ("que rien ne soit perdu") and 6:39 ("que je ne perde rien"), the echo noted in meaning decision m1; "périr" would break it. "Demeurer" is the book-wide word for "remain" (6:56; 15:4). Readable uses the plainest words for food that spoils and food that lasts.

decisions.choice: c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que ... a marqué de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sceau (L, B); a mis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sceau sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} (R)
decisions.reason: "Lui" is the Son and "son sceau" the Father’s seal, so both take the deity_pronoun setting; French keeps the Greek emphasis on "this one" with "c’est lui que".

decisions.reason: "인자" is the title in Korean Bibles (style guide), but its Sino-Korean form is opaque to new readers, so Readable glosses it once in the passage.

decisions.reason: "인치다" is old church language; Balanced uses the plain phrase with the honorific reflexive "당신" for God, Readable compares it with a stamp.

decisions.reason: As the English: Literal and Balanced keep "permanecer", John's recurring word (6:56; 15:4), and Readable uses the plainest words for food that spoils and food that lasts.

decisions.choice: one work, not many

decisions.choice: believe in the one he sent: keep trusting the one God sent

decisions.choice: they ask for a sign, the day after the feeding
decisions.reason: They had eaten the bread the day before and called it a sign (6:14). Now they want more, and 6:31 shows what they have in mind: Moses gave bread from heaven for forty years in the wilderness, not one meal. The demand for a sign is the same as in 2:18 (compare 4:48).

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, you as against Moses
decisions.reason: The pronoun σὺ is written out, which makes it emphatic. The contrast with Moses comes in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: believe you: believe what you say
decisions.reason: With a plain dative, "believe" means to accept a person's word as true. Jesus spoke of believing "in" the one God sent (6:29); the crowd offers only to believe his claim if he proves it.

decisions.choice: perform (B); show us (R)
decisions.reason: "Do a sign" is not natural English. Readable turns the purpose clause into a promise, "If we see it, we will believe you", which is what the crowd means.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The emphatic "tú" (meaning decision m2) is a stressed pronoun for Christ and takes the setting. "Te creamos" is "creer a": believe what he says (m3).

decisions.choice: the quotation runs on to the end of 6:31
decisions.reason: The crowd's words continue through 6:31, so the quotation stays open. (The English closes it at the end of this verse.)

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} (L, B); nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} croyions (L, B), nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} croirons (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is emphatic (meaning decision m2), which French shows with a stressed "toi" at Literal and Balanced. "Croire quelqu’un" means to accept what he says, as the Greek dative does (m3); "croire en" is kept for putting one’s trust in a person, as in 6:29.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for the emphatic "you" (sy) and "you" (soi)
decisions.reason: Korean does not use "당신" to a respected person face to face; the respectful title stands in for the pronoun, as it does in ordinary speech. It is not bracketed, since it replaces a word in the Greek rather than adding one.

decisions.reason: Jesus told them to work (6:27) and spoke of the work of God (6:29). Now they ask what work he himself does. The verb is the one Jesus used in 5:17: "My Father has been at work right up to now, and I am at work as well."

decisions.choice: the manna passages: Psalm 78:24; Exodus 16:4, 15; Nehemiah 9:15
decisions.reason: The words are not an exact quotation of any one verse. Psalm 78:24 says God rained down manna for them to eat and gave them the grain of heaven; in Exodus 16:4 God says, "I will rain bread from heaven for you", and in 16:15 Moses tells the people that the manna is bread the LORD has given them; Nehemiah 9:15 recalls it in prayer. The whole of Jesus's answer in 6:32-58 works through this one sentence: who gave, what the bread from heaven is, and what eating it means.

decisions.choice: he gave: God, in Scripture; the crowd may be thinking of Moses
decisions.reason: In every passage quoted it is God who gives the manna. But Jesus answers "it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven" (6:32), so the crowd seems to credit Moses, or to hold up Moses as the prophet a new sign must match.

decisions.choice: the hope of manna again
decisions.reason: Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like him (Deuteronomy 18:15), and the crowd had just called Jesus "the prophet" (6:14). A Jewish writing from about the end of the first century, 2 Baruch 29:8, says that when the Messiah comes the store of manna will come down from on high again. Feeding a crowd once falls short, in their eyes, of Moses's forty years.

decisions.choice: not Moses: the giver of the manna was God
decisions.reason: The word "not" stands first, against "Moses". Moses himself told Israel that the manna was bread given by the LORD (Exodus 16:15). Jesus corrects the crowd's reading of the verse they quoted (6:31).

decisions.choice: has given ... gives: the old gift and the gift being given now
decisions.reason: The first verb is a perfect, looking back at the manna; the second is a present: the Father is giving the true bread now, to "you", the people standing before Jesus. He is the one who calls God "my Father" (5:17-18).

decisions.choice: true: real, the reality the manna pointed to
decisions.reason: ἀληθινόν means genuine, the real thing, as with the true light (1:9) and the true vine (15:1). The manna was real food, but it was a sign of the bread that gives life to the world (6:33). The Greek puts "the true" last, for weight.

decisions.choice: Moses was not the one who gave ... my Father is the one who gives (B, R)
alternatives: not Moses has given ... but my Father gives (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the contrast between the two givers by naming each one first, in the same pattern. Balanced puts "true" before "bread" as English does; Literal keeps it at the end.

decisions.choice: no fue Moisés quien ... es mi Padre quien
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps the contrast between the two givers by naming each first.

decisions.choice: le pain du ciel, le véritable (L); le vrai pain du ciel (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the true" at the end, where the Greek puts it for weight (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable put "vrai" before the noun, where French puts it in the sense of "real, genuine".

decisions.choice: "하늘에서 [온] 빵", "하늘에서 [오는] 참된 빵"
decisions.reason: Korean cannot attach "from heaven" to a noun without a verb; Literal brackets the verb, keeping the past (the manna) against the present (the bread now given).

decisions.choice: the bread that comes down
decisions.reason: The Greek participle can refer back to "bread" (that which comes down) or stand for a person (he who comes down). The crowd takes it as bread, since they ask for some (6:34), and the sentence describes what kind of bread God gives. Only in 6:35 does Jesus say "I am the bread", and in 6:38 "I have come down from heaven"; the wording here prepares for that without yet saying it.

decisions.choice: comes down from heaven: like the manna, and like the Son
decisions.reason: The manna came down on the camp with the dew (Numbers 11:9). The same verb is used of the Son of Man, who came down from heaven (3:13), and Jesus will say it of himself in 6:38, 41, 50-51.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, not one nation
decisions.reason: The manna fed Israel in the wilderness; this bread gives life to the world, all people, as in 3:16 and 4:42 ("the Savior of the world").

decisions.choice: the bread that
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "bread" so the reader follows the sense chosen in meaning decision m1. Literal keeps "[the one]" and Balanced "the one that", which say no more than the Greek.

decisions.choice: el que baja
decisions.reason: Spanish "el que" can mean "the bread that" or "he who", as the Greek participle can (meaning decision m1), so Literal and Balanced keep both readings; Readable repeats "pan", as the English does.

decisions.choice: celui qui descend
decisions.reason: French "celui qui" can refer back to "le pain", a masculine noun, or stand for a person, so Literal and Balanced keep the openness of the Greek, where the crowd hears bread and the reader may already hear Jesus (meaning decision m1). Readable repeats "le pain", as the English does.

decisions.choice: yule anayeshuka (L); ule unaoshuka (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean "the bread that comes down" or "the one who comes down". Literal keeps the person in view with the personal "yule anayeshuka", which Swahili must choose between; Balanced and Readable keep the bread's own agreement ("ule unaoshuka"), as the meaning note reads it.

decisions.choice: "것" (L); "빵" (B, R): the bread that comes down
decisions.reason: Korean must choose between a thing ("것") and a person ("이"); the meaning decision reads "the bread that comes down", so Korean does not yet point to Jesus as a person, as the crowd's reply in 6:34 shows.

decisions.choice: "[bánh] từ trời xuống" (L); "bánh từ trời xuống" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot leave the Greek participle open: "Đấng" would name a person, "bánh" the bread. Every level follows meaning decision m1 (the bread), which the crowd's request in 6:34 supports; the footnote there gives the personal reading.

decisions.choice: o que desce (L); aquele que desce (B)
decisions.reason: Like the Greek participle, Portuguese "o que" and "aquele que" can point back to "o pão" or to a person (meaning decision m1), so Literal and Balanced need no bracket and keep the ambiguity; Readable repeats "pão", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Sir: a respectful address
alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Κύριε is the polite form used to anyone of standing. The crowd does not yet know who Jesus is; within a few sentences they grumble at him (6:41). A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: they ask for bread as the Samaritan woman asked for water
decisions.reason: The request is almost the same as hers: "Sir, give me this water!" (4:15). Like her, they think of a gift that would meet ordinary needs for good, as the manna came every day (Exodus 16:4, 35).

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for those who do not yet know who Jesus is (meaning decision m1; see docs/john-terms.md).

decisions.choice: all the time (B); every day from now on (R)
decisions.reason: "Always" here means without stopping, like the daily manna. Readable adds "please" for the tone of a request.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: As at 4:11 and 5:7: Spanish "señor" is both the polite "sir" and "Lord" (meaning decision m1). Here it is the polite address.

decisions.choice: Monsieur
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for those who do not yet know who Jesus is (meaning decision m1, whose footnote gives "Lord"); "Seigneur" would put a confession of faith in the mouth of a crowd that grumbles at him a few verses later. People still say "tu" to him, as the French brief does throughout; a native reviewer should check that "Monsieur" with "tu" does not sound odd.

decisions.choice: bwana, placed inside the sentence
decisions.reason: As in John 4 and 5: a polite "sir" from people who do not yet know who Jesus is. Placed later in the sentence, "bwana" stays lowercase. Peter's "Lord" in verse 68 is "Bwana".

decisions.choice: "선생님" for "kyrie"
decisions.reason: The crowd does not yet know who Jesus is, so they say "선생님" (docs/john-terms.md); the meaning decision's footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy"
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "thưa ông" for kyrie from people who do not yet know Jesus. Here the same crowd has just called him "Ra-bi" and "Thầy" (6:25-30); switching to "ông" would change the relationship within one scene. "Thưa Thầy" is still a polite address, not the confession "Chúa" (meaning decision m1). A reviewer should confirm this departure.

decisions.choice: Senhor, with "tu" (dá-nos)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "senhor" covers both "sir" and "Lord", and as the first word of the address it takes a capital either way, so the English footnote's choice does not arise in the wording. The crowd uses "tu", as everyone does who speaks to Jesus (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); "o senhor" is kept for human superiors.

decisions.choice: I am the bread of life: the first of John's sayings "I am" with a picture
decisions.reason: With a predicate, "I am" is ordinary grammar (see 4:26 and 8:58 for the use without one). This is the first of seven such sayings in John: the bread of life, the light of the world (8:12), the door (10:7, 9), the good shepherd (10:11), the resurrection and the life (11:25), the way, the truth and the life (14:6), and the true vine (15:1). The "I" is written out and emphatic: the bread they asked for (6:34) is not a thing but a person.

decisions.choice: the bread of life: the bread that gives life
decisions.reason: The genitive describes what the bread does, as 6:33 has just said: it gives life to the world. 6:51 calls it "the living bread".

decisions.choice: coming and believing are one act; the double negative is emphatic
decisions.reason: The two halves say the same thing in two ways, as Hebrew poetry does: to come to Jesus is to believe in him. οὐ μή is the strongest way of saying "not", and πώποτε ("ever") adds more weight to the second half.

decisions.choice: never hunger or thirst: God's promises in Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah promises God's people that "they shall not hunger or thirst" (Isaiah 49:10), and calls the thirsty and the hungry to come and eat and live (Isaiah 55:1-3). Jesus told the Samaritan woman that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst (4:14).

decisions.choice: the bread that gives life
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the phrase (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the familiar wording, which is the plain translation.

decisions.choice: certainly not ... certainly never (L); never ... never at any time (B); never ... never ... not ever (R)
decisions.reason: Each level marks the emphatic negative (meaning decision m3) in its own register, and keeps the extra "ever" of the second half.

decisions.choice: el pan que da vida
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable states the sense of the phrase (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: jamás ... nunca jamás
decisions.reason: Each level marks the emphatic negative (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: le pain de vie (L, B); le pain qui donne la vie (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide French term for John, recorded here where it first appears. Readable states the sense of the phrase, as the English does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: certainement pas ... certainement jamais (L); jamais ... jamais plus (B); plus jamais ... jamais (R)
decisions.reason: Each level marks the emphatic negative (meaning decision m3) in its own register, and keeps the extra "ever" of the second half.

decisions.choice: Mimi ni mkate wa uzima
decisions.reason: With a predicate, "I am" is an ordinary statement, as the meaning note says, so Swahili uses the plain "Mimi ni". The saying keeps "mkate" (bread), the word of the whole chapter, rather than "chakula" (food), which breaks the link with the loaves.

decisions.choice: "생명의 빵" (L, B); "생명을 주는 빵" (R)
decisions.reason: The traditional "생명의 떡" uses the older word for bread (see 6:5 in this chapter); Readable spells out the genitive as the meaning decision reads it.

decisions.choice: "bánh của sự sống" (L); "bánh sự sống" (B); "bánh ban sự sống" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek genitive with "của"; Balanced uses the set phrase readers know; Readable says what it means, the bread that gives life (meaning decision). The same applies in 6:48.

decisions.choice: quem vem ... quem crê
alternatives: aqueles que vêm ... aqueles que creem
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "those who" and "people who" to stay inclusive; Portuguese "quem" already means anyone and keeps the Greek singular, so no setting or plural is needed.

decisions.choice: I told you: Jesus refers to what he has already said in substance
alternatives: a saying not recorded in the Gospel
decisions.reason: No earlier verse has these exact words. The nearest are 6:26, that they saw and did not see the signs, and 5:38-40, "you do not believe the one he sent"; it is also possible that Jesus refers to words John does not record.

decisions.choice: you have seen me (SBLGNT)
alternatives: you have seen, and do not believe (some early witnesses)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts have "me". Some early witnesses leave it out, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus and some Latin and Syriac versions; the sense would then be "you have seen [the signs]". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: seeing without believing
decisions.reason: The crowd asked for a sign "so that we may see and believe" (6:30). Jesus says they have seen more than a sign, they have seen him, and still do not believe. Compare 20:29, where Jesus calls blessed those who believe without having seen.

decisions.choice: with your own eyes
decisions.reason: Readable stresses that they have really seen him, which is the force of "both ... and" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: con sus propios ojos
decisions.reason: As in English: stresses that they have really seen him (meaning decision m3).

pt.B: Todos os que o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dá virão a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e eu jamais mandarei embora quem vier a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. \v 38 Pois eu desci do céu não para fazer a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} própria vontade, mas a vontade daquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.
pt.R: Todos os que o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dá vão vir a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. E eu nunca vou mandar embora quem vier a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. \v 38 É que eu desci do céu, não para fazer o que eu quero, mas para fazer o que quer aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.

decisions.choice: everything that: the people given to Jesus, seen as one whole
decisions.reason: πᾶν ὃ is neuter, "everything that": John speaks of all whom the Father gives as one gift, then of each person ("the one who comes"). He does the same in 6:39 and 17:2.

decisions.choice: the Father's giving and a person's coming
decisions.reason: Those the Father gives will come; Jesus will not turn away anyone who comes. The first half says that coming to Jesus rests on the Father's gift (6:44, 65; 17:6); the second, that no one who comes will be refused. The text holds both without explaining how they fit.

decisions.choice: I will never cast out: I will welcome and keep
decisions.reason: The emphatic "by no means" (οὐ μή) with "cast outside" says, by denying the opposite, that he will receive and hold on to everyone who comes. 6:39 says the same positively. Compare the man who is cast out of the synagogue, whom Jesus then seeks out (9:34-35).

decisions.choice: he came down to do the will of the one who sent him
decisions.reason: Jesus now says of himself what he said of the bread: it comes down from heaven (6:33). He gives his reason for welcoming all who come: he is not acting on his own will but on the Father's, which 6:39-40 spell out. Compare 4:34 and 5:30.

decisions.choice: Everyone
decisions.reason: In English "everything" sounds like things, not people. Balanced and Readable say "everyone", which is already inclusive; Literal keeps the neuter (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: never send away (B); never turn away (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for refusing someone who comes asking (meaning decision m3). Readable says "what I want" and "what the one who sent me wants" for "will".

decisions.choice: Todo lo que (L); Todos los que (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the neuter (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "todos", which is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: nunca rechazaré (B); nunca le daré la espalda (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for refusing someone who comes (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Tout ce que (L); Tous ceux que (B, R)
alternatives: Tout ce que at every level
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the neuter, which sees all whom the Father gives as one gift (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "tous ceux", since French "tout ce que" would sound like things.

decisions.choice: la volonté qui est la {{deity_pronoun:mienne|Mienne}}
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "the will, the mine"; the possessive pronoun for Jesus takes the deity_pronoun setting like "ma".

decisions.choice: "모든 것" (L); "사람은 모두" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek neuter (everything, the people seen as one whole); Balanced and Readable say plainly that people are meant, as the English does.

source.text: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέν μοι μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: This and is the will of the [one] having sent me, that all that he has given me not I may lose of it, but I may raise up it on the last day.

en.L: And this is the will of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I should not lose [any] of it, but should raise it up on the last day.
en.B: And the will of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is this: that I should lose nothing of all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but raise it all up on the last day.
en.R: The one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} wants this: I must not lose any of the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Instead, I will raise them all from the dead on the last day.

es.L: Y esta es la voluntad del que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió: que de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado no pierda nada, sino que lo resucite el último día.
es.B: Y la voluntad del que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió es esta: que no pierda nada de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado, sino que lo resucite todo el último día.
es.R: El que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió quiere esto: que yo no pierda a ninguno de los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado. Al contrario, los resucitaré a todos el último día.

fr.L: Et voici la volonté de celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé : que tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donné, je n’en perde [rien], mais que je le ressuscite au dernier jour.
fr.B: Et la volonté de celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, c’est que je ne perde rien de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a donné, mais que je le ressuscite tout entier au dernier jour.
fr.R: Celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé veut ceci : je ne dois perdre aucune des personnes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a données. Au contraire, je les ressusciterai toutes au dernier jour.

sw.L: Na haya ndiyo mapenzi ya yule aliyenituma, kwamba kila kitu alichonipa nisipoteze [chochote] katika hicho, bali nikiinue siku ya mwisho.
sw.B: Na mapenzi ya yule aliyenituma ni haya: nisipoteze chochote katika yote aliyonipa, bali niyafufue yote siku ya mwisho.
sw.R: Yule aliyenituma anataka hivi: nisimpoteze hata mmoja wa watu aliyonipa. Badala yake, nitawafufua wote kutoka kwa wafu siku ya mwisho.

vi.L: Và đây là ý muốn của Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: tất cả những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không để mất [chút nào] trong đó, nhưng làm cho [tất cả] sống lại vào ngày sau cùng.
vi.B: Ý muốn của Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thế này: trong tất cả những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không để mất ai cả, nhưng sẽ làm cho tất cả sống lại vào ngày sau cùng.
vi.R: Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn thế này: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không được để mất một người nào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Trái lại, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho tất cả họ sống lại từ cõi chết vào ngày sau cùng.

ko.L: 나를 보내신 분의 뜻은 이것이다. 곧 그분께서 나에게 주신 모든 것 가운데 [하나도] 내가 잃지 않고, 마지막 날에 그것을 다시 살리는 것이다.
ko.B: 나를 보내신 분의 뜻은 이것이다. 그분께서 나에게 주신 모든 것을 내가 하나도 잃지 않고, 마지막 날에 모두 다시 살리는 것이다.
ko.R: 나를 보내신 분께서는 이것을 원하신다. 그분께서 나에게 주신 사람들을 내가 한 사람도 잃지 않는 것이다. 오히려 나는 마지막 날에 그들을 모두 죽은 사람들 가운데서 다시 살릴 것이다.

pt.L: E esta é a vontade daquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou: que tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu, eu não perca [nada] disso, mas o ressuscite no último dia.
pt.B: E a vontade daquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou é esta: que eu não perca nada de tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu, mas que ressuscite tudo no último dia.
pt.R: Aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou quer isto: que eu não perca nenhuma das pessoas que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu. Pelo contrário, eu vou ressuscitar todas elas no último dia.

decisions.choice: all that he has given me ... it: the whole people given, as in 6:37
decisions.reason: The neuter "all that" is picked up by "it" twice: not one part of the Father's gift will be lost, and all of it will be raised.

decisions.choice: lose: let perish
decisions.reason: ἀπολέσω is the verb of the leftover pieces in 6:12 ("so that nothing is lost") and of the food that perishes in 6:27; with people it means to perish, as in 3:16. What Jesus did with the bread, he does with those given to him.

decisions.choice: raise up on the last day: the bodily resurrection at the end
decisions.reason: The "last day" is the day of resurrection and judgment (11:24; 12:48). The phrase comes four times in this chapter (6:39, 40, 44, 54). John holds together life that starts now (6:40, 47) and raising at the end, as in 5:24-29.

decisions.choice: it all
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "all" so "it" clearly means the whole of what was given (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: them ... raise them all from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant by "it" and says what raising means here (meaning decision m3). The same wording is used for the refrain in 6:40.

decisions.choice: perder; el último día
decisions.reason: "Perder" is the verb of 6:12 and 6:27 (meaning decision m2). "El último día" is the plain wording; "el día postrero" now sounds old.

decisions.choice: ninguno de los que ... los resucitaré a todos
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the people meant (meaning decision m1). Spanish "resucitar" already means to raise from the dead.

decisions.choice: perdre; ressusciter
decisions.reason: "Perdre" is the verb of 6:12 and 6:27 at every level, so what Jesus did with the bread is seen in what he does with those given to him (meaning decision m2). "Ressusciter" says "raise from the dead" in one word, so Readable needs no added "from the dead"; it says "les ... toutes" for the people meant by "it" (m1).

decisions.choice: "다시 살리다" (raise up)
decisions.reason: "다시 살리다" says plainly that the dead are raised to life; Readable adds "죽은 사람들 가운데서" as the English Readable adds "from the dead".

source.text: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐγὼ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: This for is the will of the Father of me, that everyone the [one] looking on the Son and believing in him may have life eternal, and will raise up him I on the last day."

en.L: For this is the will of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} should have eternal life, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will raise {{gender:them|him}} up on the last day."
en.B: For what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father wills is this: everyone who sees the Son and believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will have eternal life, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will raise {{gender:them|him}} up on the last day."
en.R: My Father wants everyone who sees the Son and believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to have eternal life. And I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will raise {{gender:them|him}} from the dead on the last day."

es.L: Porque esta es la voluntad de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre: que todo el que mira al Hijo y cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenga vida eterna, y yo mismo lo resucitaré el último día».
es.B: Porque lo que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre quiere es esto: que todo el que ve al Hijo y cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenga vida eterna, y yo mismo lo resucitaré el último día».
es.R: Mi Padre quiere que todos los que ven al Hijo y creen en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tengan vida eterna. Y yo mismo los resucitaré el último día».

fr.L: Car voici la volonté de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père : que quiconque contemple le Fils et croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ait la vie éternelle ; et je le ressusciterai, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, au dernier jour. »
fr.B: Car ce que veut {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, c’est que quiconque voit le Fils et croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ait la vie éternelle ; et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je le ressusciterai au dernier jour. »
fr.R: Mon Père veut que tous ceux qui voient le Fils et croient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} aient la vie éternelle. Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je les ressusciterai au dernier jour. »

sw.L: Kwa sababu hili ndilo analolitaka Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}: kila mtu anayemtazama Mwana na kumwamini awe na uzima wa milele, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitamwinua siku ya mwisho."
sw.B: Kwa maana Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anataka hivi: kila anayemwona Mwana na kumwamini atakuwa na uzima wa milele, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitamfufua siku ya mwisho."
sw.R: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anataka kila mtu anayemwona Mwana na kumwamini apate uzima wa milele. Nami {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitamfufua kutoka kwa wafu siku ya mwisho."

vi.L: Vì đây là ý muốn của Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: ai nhìn xem Con và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thì có sự sống đời đời, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho người ấy sống lại vào ngày sau cùng."
vi.B: Vì ý muốn của Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là: ai thấy Con và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thì được sự sống đời đời, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho người ấy sống lại vào ngày sau cùng."
vi.R: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn mọi người thấy Con và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều có sự sống đời đời. Và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho họ sống lại từ cõi chết vào ngày sau cùng."

ko.L: 내 아버지의 뜻은 이것이다. 곧 아들을 바라보고 그를 믿는 사람은 모두 영원한 생명을 얻는 것이다. 그리고 나 자신이 마지막 날에 그 사람을 다시 살릴 것이다."
ko.B: 내 아버지께서 원하시는 것은 이것이다. 아들을 보고 그를 믿는 사람은 누구나 영원한 생명을 얻는 것이다. 그리고 나 자신이 마지막 날에 그 사람을 다시 살릴 것이다."
ko.R: 내 아버지께서는 아들을 보고 믿는 사람이 모두 영원한 생명을 얻기를 원하신다. 그리고 나는 마지막 날에 그 사람을 직접 죽은 사람들 가운데서 다시 살릴 것이다."

pt.L: Pois esta é a vontade do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai: que todo aquele que contempla o Filho e crê {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} tenha vida eterna, e eu mesmo o ressuscitarei no último dia."
pt.B: Pois o que o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai quer é isto: todo aquele que vê o Filho e crê {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} terá a vida eterna, e eu mesmo o ressuscitarei no último dia."
pt.R: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai quer que todos os que veem o Filho e acreditam {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} tenham a vida eterna. E eu mesmo vou ressuscitar essas pessoas no último dia."

decisions.choice: looks on the Son: sees him with attention, and so comes to believe
decisions.reason: θεωρῶν means to look at something with attention. It is not the seeing of 6:36, where the crowd saw and did not believe; here looking and believing go together. In 3:14-15 Jesus compared himself to the bronze serpent, which the bitten Israelites looked at and lived (Numbers 21:8-9).

decisions.choice: has eternal life now, and will be raised on the last day
decisions.reason: The will of the Father is that the one who believes should have eternal life, a present possession (5:24), and that Jesus should raise that person on the last day. The two are not alternatives: life starts now and is completed at the resurrection.

decisions.choice: I myself will raise
decisions.reason: The pronoun ἐγὼ is written out, which makes it emphatic: Jesus himself will raise the dead, the work 5:21 and 5:25-29 give to the Son.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Him" refers to "everyone who looks on the Son", men and women alike, so it takes the gender setting. "Him" in "believes in him" is the Son and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: sees
decisions.reason: The everyday word. Readable turns "this is the will of my Father, that" into "My Father wants", as in 6:39, and says "from the dead" for the raising.

decisions.choice: lo resucitaré, no gender setting
decisions.reason: After "todo el que", Spanish refers back with the ordinary clitic "lo", which is general here; Readable uses the plural. No setting is needed.

decisions.choice: quiconque ... je le ressusciterai (L, B); tous ceux ... je les ressusciterai (R)
decisions.reason: The English needs the gender setting for "him". French "quiconque" already includes men and women, and the pronoun "le" that picks it up is grammatical, not a statement about men, so no setting is needed; Readable uses the plural, as the Spanish does. "Lui" is the Son and takes the deity_pronoun setting, and the emphatic "moi" (meaning decision m3) does too.

decisions.choice: contemple (L); voit (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "contempler" for this verb of attentive looking (meaning decision m1), as in 1:14 and 1:32; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "voir".

decisions.choice: nitamwinua (L); nitamfufua (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "raise up" is the ordinary word for making someone stand up. Literal says "kumwinua" (lift him up) in verses 39, 40, 44 and 54; Balanced and Readable say "kumfufua" (raise from the dead), which is what the meaning note says it means.

decisions.choice: "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "그 사람" (that person) is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change; "그" alone tends to be heard as male.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" (L, B); "họ" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người ấy" and "họ" do not mark gender, so the English gender setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: o (L, B); essas pessoas (R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting for "them/him". In Portuguese the "o" that refers back to "todo aquele que" is ordinary generic Portuguese and includes women (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7); Readable says "essas pessoas". The English span on "myself" has no counterpart: "eu mesmo" takes none.
